title: Puncture localization identifies H¹ with derived torsion
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $\mathfrak m$ its maximal ideal, and $W$ an open of $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] containing exactly the points other than the closed point. There is an additive equivalence $H^1(W,\mathcal O_W)\cong R^2\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(R)$, where the left side is Modules.H of the unit structure module and $\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}$ is the functor [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor].

proof.text: A prime containing the maximal ideal equals that ideal, so W is X minus V(m). Take an injective R-module resolution R → E. The associated quasi-coherent sheaves of injective modules are flasque over the Noetherian affine scheme, and hence their restrictions compute the sheaf cohomology of the restricted structure sheaf.

The kernel of E^k=Γ(X,tilde E^k) → Γ(W,tilde E^k) is Γ_m(E^k). Indeed, using finite generators f_i of m, a section restricts to zero precisely when each of its images in (E^k)_(f_i) is zero. There are exponents e_i with f_i^e_i x=0; a power of m of exponent at least the sum of the e_i annihilates x. Conversely m-power torsion localizes to zero on all D(f_i). Flasqueness gives surjectivity, hence a short exact sequence of complexes with left term Γ_m(E).

The middle complex resolves R, so its degree-one and degree-two cohomology vanish. The localization long exact sequence gives H¹(W,O_W) ≅ H²(Γ_m(E)), which is R²Γ_m(R). Identify the underlying additive sheaf of the unit structure module with O_W. If W is empty the restriction complex is zero, and the same exact sequence applies.
